content_units: Weekly Delivery Snapshot
Using a simple RAG label:
-   Green   = on track
-   Amber   = at risk
-   Red   = needs immediate escalation
Status logic used here weighs progress gap, blocked days, issue count, and severity.
Workstream RAG Assessment
Workstream   Planned %   Actual %   Variance   Blocked Days   Open Issues   Severity   RAG   Status Note
Backend API   80   78   -2   1   4   medium     Green     Slightly behind, but variance is small and blockers are limited
Mobile App   75   60   -15   4   9   high     Red     Material schedule slip with sustained blocking and high issue pressure
Data Migration   50   52   +2   0   2   low     Green     Ahead of plan with low issue load and no blocking
QA Automation   65   58   -7   2   6   medium     Amber     Noticeable delay and moderate blocker volume; recovery still feasible
Risk Priorities and What They Mean
-   On track:     Backend API, Data Migration
-   At risk:     QA Automation
-   Needs immediate escalation:     Mobile App
Most concerning signals
-   Mobile App   is the clearest escalation case: largest progress gap, most blocked days, most open issues, and   high   severity.
-   QA Automation   is not yet critical, but trend signals show delivery risk if not corrected this week.
-   Backend API   is slightly behind but still operating within manageable tolerance.
Top 3 Blockers and Best Next Action
1) Mobile App — sustained delivery blockage
-   Why it matters:   4 blocked days, 9 open issues, and a 15-point progress shortfall make this the biggest threat to milestone delivery.
-   Most important action:   Run an immediate escalation review with engineering lead/product owner to remove the top dependency and cut scope to must-have items for the week.
2) QA Automation — coverage lag affecting release confidence
-   Why it matters:   7-point progress gap plus 2 blocked days and 6 open issues can slow validation and create downstream release risk.
-   Most important action:   Reprioritize automation to the highest-risk test paths only and assign temporary support from Backend/API or QA manual testers.
3) Backend API — minor slippage that could spread
-   Why it matters:   Only slightly behind now, but unresolved medium-severity issues could affect dependent teams if left open.
-   Most important action:   Close the top 1–2 dependency-related issues this week to prevent impact on Mobile App and QA Automation.
Quick Actions
Escalate Mobile
Review Risks
Supporting Notes
Context used:
-   Progress variance   = actual progress minus planned progress
- High blocked days + high severity + large variance were treated as strongest escalation indicators
- Data Migration was kept   Green   because it is ahead of plan, unblocked, and carrying low issue volume
